# Oglets

> Oglets (oglets.swymble.com) is a single-screen web toy. An Oglet is a small
> creature made mostly of eyes, drawn from a weighted genome. You are given one
> the first time you open the page, it is kept in your browser, and it is yours.

The site has three pages, reached from the bar at the top: Home, World, Genome.

**Home** is the landing page, and it is deliberately almost empty: the word
*oglets*, whose O is an eye that follows your cursor and blinks, and a single
Enter button. A first-time visitor lands here; a returning one is taken straight
to their Oglet.

**World** is the live canvas. Your Oglet watches your cursor, follows it, leans
toward you when it is fond of you and backs off if you have been jabbing it.
Drag it, or tap it once to say hello. Left alone it entertains itself — it
tracks a speck only it can see, daydreams, or goes to check the last place your
cursor was — and then naps. Come back and it greets you.

Its expressions are driven, never random: it is happy when you hold it, when you
greet it or when it is playing; cross when it is mashed; sad only when you are
on the page and not coming near. An Oglet alone is perfectly content on its own.

**Genome** is your Oglet's own page, and then every mutation it could have been
drawn with. It shows the creature at size, its name, its four traits as tags
with how often each occurs, its rarity — scored one trait at a time across seven
tiers from Common to God — the true odds of its exact combination, and its ID.
Below that are all 59 mutations across four genes — eye shape, pupil, eye
colour and pupil colour — each a live drawing with its tier, star rating and how common
it is. Open one and it tells you where it is supposed to have come from.
Mutations you have not met yet stay hidden until you do.

The eye shapes are Round, Egg, Bean, Capsule, Dome, Arch, Block, Diamond, Slab,
Bud, Wedge and Sphere (a genuinely three-dimensional eye, lit and shaded). The pupils are Dot, Oval, Slit, Bar, Ring, Square, Rhomb,
Cross, Spark, Target and Heart. Eye colour and pupil colour are separate genes,
so an unusual pupil colour can turn up on an ordinary eye.

Ten mutations belong to the **God line**: mutations that are renderings rather
than values, rarer than one roll in a hundred thousand, and each making its
Oglet God rarity on its own. They are Pixel (the whole creature
redrawn as a grid of 22 chunky pixels), Glitch (the picture of it tearing into
displaced bands with the colour channels pulling apart),
Hypnotic (a pupil that is a turning spiral), Eclipse (a pupil that is a
black disc inside a corona of streamers), Veins (a bloodshot eye), Cosmos (an eye with a nebula and
drifting stars behind it in three parallax layers), Chimera and Discord (the two
eyes, or the two pupils, holding different colours), and Prism and Spectrum
(the eye or the pupil cycling through every colour at once).

An Oglet **is** a hash: 128 random bits, written as 32 characters, generated
once in your browser and belonging to nobody else. That ID always redraws the
same creature, which is what makes it verifiable without any server keeping a
record of it. Its name is derived from the ID rather than stored, so the same
Oglet is called the same thing anywhere it is ever opened.

Rarity is not a lookup table — a trait is rare because its allele is rare, and
an Oglet is rare because its traits are.

Everything runs client-side on one canvas and a set of plain ES modules. No
accounts, no network calls, no tracking; the only thing stored is your Oglet's
ID in this browser.

Oglets is part of SWYMBLE Labs, the experiments arm of the SWYMBLE software
studio.
